exercises.en: This meat is pork.
exercises.why: After a noun ending in a vowel, use 예요.

exercises.en: This is a factory.
exercises.why: After a noun ending in a consonant, use 이에요.

exercises.en: That place was a theater.
exercises.why: Past of 이다 after a consonant is 이었어요.

exercises.en: That person was my friend.
exercises.why: After a vowel, 이었어요 shrinks to 였어요.

exercises.en: I will introduce my friend tomorrow.
exercises.why: Future is stem + ㄹ/을 거예요, and 하 ends in a vowel so it takes ㄹ.

exercises.en: It will be very cold tomorrow.
exercises.why: 춥다 is ㅂ irregular: ㅂ becomes 우 before 을, giving 추울.

exercises.en: I will live in Seoul.
exercises.why: A stem ending in ㄹ just keeps its ㄹ: 살 거예요.

exercises.en: I bought food to eat tomorrow.
exercises.why: ~을 before a noun describes something that will happen.

exercises.en: That was my passport.
I will visit Seoul tomorrow.
I will play soccer tomorrow.
This place is not a theater.

reading.ko: 저는 민수예요. 저는 회사원이에요. 어제는 토요일이었어요. 저는 극장에서 영화를 봤어요. 영화는 아주 재미있었어요. 내일은 친구를 방문할 거예요. 우리는 친구 집에서 돼지고기를 먹을 거예요.
reading.en: I am Minsu. I am an office worker. Yesterday was Saturday. I watched a movie at the theater. The movie was very fun. Tomorrow I will visit a friend. We will eat pork at my friend's house.

questions.q: What is Minsu's job?
What did Minsu do yesterday?
questions.a: He watched a movie at the theater.

questions.q: What will they eat tomorrow?

exercises.en: Three coffees, please.
exercises.why: Before a counter, 셋 becomes 세.

exercises.en: There are twenty students in the classroom.
exercises.why: Before a counter, 스물 becomes 스무.

exercises.en: These flowers are 5,000 won.
exercises.why: Money uses Sino-Korean numbers: 오천.

exercises.en: I watched that movie twice.
exercises.why: 번 takes pure Korean numbers, and 둘 becomes 두 before it.

exercises.en: It is 4:30 now.
exercises.why: Hours use pure Korean numbers, and 넷 becomes 네 before 시.

exercises.en: Class starts at 9:15.
exercises.why: Minutes use Sino-Korean numbers.

exercises.en: My younger sibling is eight years old.
exercises.why: Age with 살 uses pure Korean numbers.

exercises.en: Today is my first class.
exercises.why: "First" is 첫 번째, not 한 번째.

exercises.en: I have three younger siblings.
I bought two apples.
It is 2:10 now.
I am thirty years old.

reading.ko: 저는 스물다섯 살이에요. 저는 회사원이에요. 우리 회사에는 사람이 열두 명 있어요. 회사에 차도 두 대 있어요. 저는 아침 여덟 시에 회사에 가요. 오늘 저는 커피 세 잔을 샀어요. 커피 세 잔은 만 이천 원이었어요.
reading.en: I am twenty-five years old. I am an office worker. There are twelve people at our company. The company also has two cars. I go to the office at eight in the morning. Today I bought three coffees. The three coffees were 12,000 won.

questions.q: How old is the writer?
How many people work at the company?
How much did the coffees cost?

exercises.en: We were in Busan for two days.
exercises.why: 동안 after a length of time means "for".

exercises.en: I ran for two hours yesterday.
exercises.why: 시간 for duration takes pure Korean numbers.

exercises.en: I lived in Korea for three months.
exercises.why: 개월 takes Sino-Korean numbers.

exercises.en: I will go to Korea next year.
exercises.why: 지난/다음 can't go with 년; "next year" is 내년.

exercises.en: I will go to Japan next month.
exercises.why: "Next month" is 다음 달.

exercises.en: My birthday is June 10th.
exercises.why: June is spelled 유월, not 육월.

exercises.en: I exercise three times a week.
exercises.why: Time unit + 에 means "per".

exercises.en: I rested at home for one day.
exercises.why: "One day" as a span is 하루.

exercises.en: I studied Korean for two years.
exercises.ko: 저는 이 년 동안 한국어를 공부했어요.

exercises.en: I drink coffee twice a day.
exercises.ko: 저는 하루에 커피를 두 번 마셔요.

exercises.en: I have plans next week.
I usually drive for one hour.
exercises.ko: 저는 보통 한 시간 동안 운전해요.

reading.ko: 저는 요리사예요. 저는 하루에 열 시간 일해요. 일요일에는 일하지 않아요. 작년에 저는 일본에서 육 개월 동안 살았어요. 일본에서 일본 요리를 배웠어요. 내년에는 한국 요리를 배울 거예요.
reading.en: I am a chef. I work ten hours a day. I don't work on Sundays. Last year I lived in Japan for six months. I learned Japanese cooking in Japan. Next year I will learn Korean cooking.

questions.q: How many hours a day does the writer work?
How long did the writer live in Japan?
What will the writer learn next year?

exercises.en: I only drank coffee in the morning.
exercises.why: ~만 means "only" and replaces 을/를.

exercises.en: That actor came from America.
exercises.why: ~에서 marks the place something comes from.

exercises.ko: 수업은 아홉 시___ 열두 시까지 해요.
exercises.en: Class runs from nine to twelve.
exercises.why: ~부터 marks a starting time.

exercises.en: I go from Seoul to Busan by train.
exercises.why: ~까지 marks the end point.

exercises.en: I go to school by bus.
exercises.why: 버스 ends in a vowel, so use 로.

exercises.en: I ate the bread with my hands.
exercises.why: 손 ends in a consonant (not ㄹ), so use 으로.

exercises.en: We went to the theater by subway.
exercises.why: After ㄹ, use 로, not 으로.

exercises.en: How many apples did you buy?
exercises.why: 몇 + counter asks "how many".

exercises.en: I work from Monday to Friday.
The train departed from Busan.
I only study at the library.
The store assistant came out of the room.

reading.ko: 저는 미국에서 왔어요. 지금 서울에서 한국어를 공부해요. 수업은 월요일부터 금요일까지 있어요. 저는 지하철로 학교에 가요. 교실에서는 한국어로만 말해요. 토요일에는 친구들이 우리 집에 와요.
reading.en: I came from America. Now I study Korean in Seoul. I have class from Monday to Friday. I go to school by subway. In the classroom I speak only in Korean. On Saturdays my friends come to my house.

questions.q: Where is the writer from?
How does the writer get to school?
What language does the writer use in the classroom?

exercises.en: I bought green tea and bread.
exercises.why: 녹차 ends in a vowel, so use 와.

exercises.en: There is medicine and water on the desk.
exercises.why: 약 ends in a consonant, so use 과.

exercises.en: I listened to music with my younger sibling.
exercises.why: 동생 ends in a consonant, so use 이랑.

exercises.en: I sent a letter to my friend.
exercises.why: Use 에게 for a person you send something to; 에 is for places.

exercises.en: I gave flowers to my grandmother.
exercises.why: 께 is the honorific "to" for respected people.

exercises.en: I received a present from my friend.
exercises.why: 한테서 means "from" a person; 에서 is for places.

exercises.en: I prepared bread for Mom.
exercises.why: 을/를 위해서 means "for the sake of".

exercises.en: We talked about that movie.
exercises.why: "About" is noun + 에 대해서.

exercises.en: I ate lunch with my friend.
I received a letter from my friend.
We talked about music.
I gave green tea to my friend.

reading.ko: 오늘은 엄마 생일이에요. 저는 아침 여섯 시에 일어났어요. 저는 동생하고 같이 엄마를 위해서 아침을 준비했어요. 우리는 빵과 녹차를 준비했어요. 저는 엄마께 꽃을 드렸어요. 동생은 엄마께 편지를 드렸어요. 오늘은 정말 좋은 날이에요.
reading.en: Today is Mom's birthday. I got up at six in the morning. With my younger sibling, I prepared breakfast for Mom. We prepared bread and green tea. I gave Mom flowers. My younger sibling gave Mom a letter. Today is a really good day.

questions.q: Whose birthday is it?
What did they prepare for breakfast?
What did the younger sibling give Mom?

exercises.en: In this class, books are provided.
exercises.why: 하다 → 되다 makes the passive, and 되어요 contracts to 돼요.

exercises.en: That student is respected by friends.
exercises.why: 존경하다 becomes passive with 받다.

exercises.en: The window opened.
exercises.why: The passive of 열다 is 열리다.

exercises.en: The shop door was closed.
exercises.why: The passive of 닫다 is 닫히다.

exercises.en: The vacuum cleaner is broken.
exercises.why: 나다 describes something happening by itself.

exercises.en: I broke the vacuum cleaner.
exercises.why: 내다 means someone caused it, so it takes an object with 을/를.

exercises.en: The TV turned on.
exercises.why: 켜다 + 어지다 makes the passive 켜지다.

exercises.en: The light went off at night.
exercises.why: 끄다 + 어지다 becomes 꺼지다 (ㅡ drops).

exercises.en: The room was locked.
I turned on the light.
A strange smell is coming from the room.
The box was placed on the chair.

reading.ko: 어제 저는 늦게 집에 왔어요. 방에 들어갔어요. 하지만 불이 켜지지 않았어요. 방에서 이상한 냄새도 났어요. 저는 짜증이 났어요. 저는 창문을 열었어요. 시원한 바람이 들어왔어요.
reading.en: Yesterday I came home late. I went into my room. But the light didn't turn on. There was also a strange smell in the room. I got annoyed. I opened the window. A cool wind came in.

questions.q: What was wrong with the light?
What did the writer notice in the room?
What did the writer open?

exercises.en: I like this picture.
exercises.why: 좋다 is an adjective, so the liked thing takes 이/가, and 그림 ends in a consonant.

exercises.en: My cousin dislikes beer.
exercises.why: With an object marked 을/를, use the verb 싫어하다.

exercises.en: I like that picture.
exercises.why: 마음에 들다 means "to be to one's liking"; 들다 → 들어요.

exercises.en: I went back home at five.
exercises.why: 돌다 + 가다 makes the compound verb 돌아가다.

exercises.en: My friend gave my book back.
exercises.why: "Give back" is 돌려주다.

exercises.en: My personality is different from my younger sibling's.
exercises.why: Compare with 와/과 + 다르다; 성격 ends in a consonant.

exercises.en: It takes one hour from home to the office.
exercises.why: 걸리다 also means "to take (time)".

exercises.en: I caught a cold.
exercises.why: Illness + 에 걸리다 means to catch it.

exercises.en: I have a fever.
My stomach hurts.
My friend brought beer.
My hobby is similar to my cousin's hobby.

reading.ko: 저는 이번 주에 독감에 걸렸어요. 열이 많이 났어요. 기침도 많이 했어요. 저는 사흘 동안 집에 있었어요. 제 사촌이 약하고 빵을 가져왔어요. 저는 사촌에게 정말 고마웠어요. 이제 저는 괜찮아요.
reading.en: I caught the flu this week. I had a high fever. I also coughed a lot. I stayed at home for three days. My cousin brought medicine and bread. I was really grateful to my cousin. Now I'm okay.

questions.q: What illness did the writer catch?
How long did the writer stay at home?
What did the cousin bring?

exercises.en: Gyeongju is a historic city.
exercises.why: Use ~적인 before a noun.

exercises.en: The subway is very economical.
exercises.why: ~적이다 ends a sentence; 적 ends in a consonant, so 이에요.

exercises.en: Personally, I like this result.
exercises.why: ~적으로 makes an adverb.

exercises.en: She explained the problem scientifically.
exercises.why: ~적으로 describes how an action is done.

exercises.en: My cat is really lovely.
exercises.why: ~스럽다 is ㅂ irregular: 스러워요.

exercises.en: That movie was really disappointing.
exercises.why: Past of ~스럽다 is ~스러웠어요.

exercises.en: This sentence isn't natural.
exercises.why: Negation is stem + 지 않다, so keep the stem 자연스럽.

exercises.en: That was a really satisfying result.
exercises.why: Before a noun, ~스럽다 becomes ~스러운.

exercises.en: Personally, I like nature.
The result was satisfying.
He is an impulsive person.
I was born in Seoul.

reading.ko: 저는 서울에서 태어났어요. 지금은 대학교에 다녀요. 저는 역사를 공부해요. 서울에는 역사적인 장소가 많아요. 저는 그 장소들에 대해서 공부해요. 공부는 힘들어요. 그러나 정말 재미있어요. 나중에 저는 역사 선생님이 될 거예요.
reading.en: I was born in Seoul. Now I attend university. I study history. There are many historic places in Seoul. I study those places. Studying is hard. However, it is really fun. Later I will become a history teacher.

questions.q: Where was the writer born?
What does the writer study?
What will the writer become later?

exercises.en: Our house is big and warm.
exercises.why: ~고 joins two descriptions with "and".

exercises.en: My younger sibling is a student, and I am an office worker.
exercises.why: After a noun ending in a consonant, use 이고.

exercises.en: I wanted to rest at home yesterday.
exercises.why: "Want to" is verb stem + 고 싶다.

exercises.en: I went to the kitchen and drank water.
exercises.why: When you go somewhere and do something there, use 가서.

exercises.en: My friend came to our house and ate dinner.
exercises.why: When you come somewhere and do something there, use 와서.

exercises.en: I sat on the chair and read the newspaper.
exercises.why: Position verbs take ~아/어서 when the next action happens in that position.

exercises.en: I lay on the sofa and watched TV.
exercises.why: 눕다 is ㅂ irregular, so ~어서 gives 누워서.

exercises.ko: 저는 이번 방학에 바다에 가___ 싶어요.
exercises.en: I want to go to the sea this vacation.
exercises.why: "Want to" is verb stem + 고 싶다.

exercises.en: I want to eat fruit.
I went to the mountain and rested.
Today the weather is nice and warm.
I miss my family.

reading.ko: 다음 주부터 방학이에요. 저는 방학에 바다에 가고 싶어요. 바다는 크고 시원해요. 저는 친구들하고 같이 바다에 가서 놀 거예요. 하지만 제 동생은 바다를 싫어해요. 동생은 산을 좋아해요.
reading.en: Vacation starts next week. I want to go to the sea during vacation. The sea is big and cool. I will go to the sea with my friends and play. But my younger sibling dislikes the sea. My sibling likes mountains.

questions.q: When does vacation start?
Where does the writer want to go?
What does the younger sibling like?
